answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a vault before its offers count, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. The stake does not prove a personhood claim; it makes spawning identities expensive: an attacker must tie up capital for each one and risks losing it on detected abuse. A garden of reputation can help route trusted work, while pigment marks flagged accounts, but neither replaces the costly, enforceable stake.
